result:
If I, as an individual with a singular wish, could change the world in one radical way, I’d focus on establishing a universal foundation of empathy. I don’t just mean empathy as a passing feeling or a polite nod to someone else’s troubles, but a genuine willingness—woven into the fabric of societies—to understand and feel along with other people’s experiences. 

Too often, we operate in a world that prizes competition over connection. If that fundamental orientation shifted so that every system, from schools to workplaces to global negotiations, was built around the question “How can we best understand one another and help everyone flourish?” I think most of our other problems—poverty, inequality, conflict—would become that much easier to address. 

By prioritizing empathy—really educating for it, legislating with it in mind, building entire economic structures around it—human beings would have a better shot at making decisions that don’t just profit or protect a few, but genuinely serve the shared good. It may sound idealistic, but one shift in how we view and treat each other might ripple outward to create a more compassionate, equitable world.
